content:
Apple TV has just added a batch of classic movies for subscribers, launching ahead of a particularly strong fall slate.

Apple TV has expanded its library with a new batch of movies ahead of its heavyweight fall lineup.

The film world has been abuzz with talk lately. Box office hits such as "Blossom Apple," "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" and "Obsession" have all sparked cultural phenomena, and the overall movie market is also showing strong momentum.

It looks like Apple wants a piece of the action too.

This week, Apple TV added a large number of acclaimed movies for subscribers to watch for free. The specific lineup varies slightly by region, but U.S. audiences can find titles such as "The Martian," "Arrival," "Eye in the Sky," "The Big Sick," "Memories of Murder" and "21 Jump Street."

With this batch of new titles added, Apple's library has nearly doubled overnight.

Apple acquiring the rights to these movies doesn't mean it has given up on its own original films. In fact, these new titles are arriving just ahead of a packed fall release schedule.

Here are six new films coming to Apple TV this fall:

  • September 4: "Mayday"
  • October 2: "The Last First: Winter K2"
  • October 9: "Matchbox The Movie"
  • October 16: "Tenzing"
  • November 13: "Being Heumann"
  • November 25: "Way of the Warrior Kid"

Apple has long been trying to strike a balance between "awards-bait films" and "mainstream entertainment." This fall, the split looks to be roughly 50-50.

"Mayday," "Matchbox" and "Way of the Warrior Kid" all look like easygoing action comedies starring the likes of Ryan Reynolds and John Cena; meanwhile, "Being Heumann," "Tenzing" and "The Last First" are clearly aiming for awards season.

Apple has consistently performed well on the television side—the recent return of "Ted Lasso" is a prime example. Whether its ambitions in film can achieve the same success remains to be seen.

Apple TV costs $12.99 per month, and can also be bundled with other services through Apple One for a discounted rate.
